title: Long cord, more loops
hook: In the paper’s setup, which length knotted more often?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: The experiment used a 30cm box, one revolution per second and ten seconds of tumbling. Its short strings had no observed knots; three-metre strings knotted in 55% of the reported trials. The stage samples those observed frequencies with seed 17.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.

recall.question: In the tumbling-box study, 3 m strings knotted in 55% of trials. What does that tell you about a 3 m cable coiled in your drawer?
options: It will knot 55% of the time too
The 55% belongs to that box setup only
It cannot knot at all unless something tumbles it
recall.why: 55% is the frequency observed in a 30 cm box turning once a second for 10 seconds. A drawer is a different box, string and motion, so that number does not transfer to it as a probability.
